sources.sections: CMB temperature anisotropies at about 380,000 years

reheating: In inflationary scenarios, field energy transfers to particles and thermalizes. Its duration, temperature and initial products depend on the reheating model; all Standard Model species need not be produced simultaneously.
uniformity: Large-scale near homogeneity is part of the cosmological reconstruction. The observed anisotropy of order 1e-5 refers to CMB temperature at last scattering, not an instantaneous uniformity measurement at reheating.
hot_plasma: For a thermalized Standard Model plasma well above the electroweak scale, all Standard Model degrees of freedom are approximately relativistic. The unbroken electroweak gauge basis is B and W^a; the low-temperature photon/Z basis is not used here.

thermal_weights.scope: Ideal relativistic equilibrium, common temperature, negligible chemical potentials; no right-handed neutrinos included.

freeze_out: Thermal freeze-out compares an interaction rate with the cosmic expansion rate. The passive register's zero-work cost barrier is a different mechanism.
